en: The Theravāda Vinaya Mahāvibhaṅga:
The Section on the Training Rules (Sekhiyakaṇḍa)
Pādukavagga 75.
The Training Rule on Defecating in Water.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the group-of-six monks were voiding excrement, urine, and spittle in water.
People complained, grumbled, and became indignant, saying:
"How can these ascetics, followers of the Sakyan, void excrement, urine, and spittle in water, just like householders who indulge in sensual pleasures?"
The bhikkhus heard those people grumbling, complaining, and criticizing.
Those bhikkhus who were of few desires... [and so on]... they grumbled, complained, and criticized:
"How can the group-of-six bhikkhus even defecate, urinate, or spit in water?"... [and so on]...
“Is it true, monks, that you discharge excrement, urine, and spittle into the water?
“It is true, Blessed One.
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them... [as before]...
"How indeed, you foolish men, can you void excrement, urine, or spittle in water?
This, foolish men, does not lead to the confidence of those without confidence...
And furthermore, monks, you should recite this training rule as follows:"
“‘I shall not discharge feces, urine, or spittle into water’—this training is to be observed.
Thus was this training rule laid down by the Blessed One for the monks.
Now at that time, sick monks were apprehensive about discharging feces, urine, or spittle into water.
They reported this matter to the Blessed One.
Then the Blessed One, having given a discourse on the Dhamma with reference to this cause and this occasion, addressed the bhikkhus:
“I allow you, bhikkhus, for a sick bhikkhu to void excrement, urine, or spittle in water.”
And furthermore, monks, you should recite this training rule thus:
“‘I will not, when not ill, discharge feces, urine, or spittle into water’—this is a training to be observed.
One who is not ill should not discharge feces, urine, or spittle into water.
Whoever, out of disrespect, not being ill, voids excrement, urine, or spittle into water, commits an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
There is no offense if it was unintentional.
In the case of one who is forgetful, one who is unaware,
or one who is ill.
When water overflows onto dry land,
in times of distress,
and for one who is insane.
One whose mind is distracted,
one overwhelmed by pain,
and one who is a first-time offender.
The fifteenth training rule is finished.
The seventh section on shoes is concluded.
Venerable sirs, the rules of training have been recited.
In this matter, I ask the venerable ones:
"Are you pure in this?
A second time I ask:
“Are you pure in this matter?
For a third time I ask:
“Are you pure in this matter?”
Venerable sirs, this matter is pure; therefore, you are silent. Thus do I understand it.
The Sekhiyas are finished.
The Section on the Sekhiyas is finished.
